prompt.brief: Design a complete container CI/CD platform that builds, tests, scans, signs, and deploys services across environments with approvals, progressive delivery, monitoring, and rollback.
successSignals: Use immutable source revisions, signed artifacts, environment policy, and a release pointer as the deployment source of truth.
Isolate untrusted build workers, cache safe dependencies, and enforce quality, vulnerability, license, and approval gates.
Deploy with health checks and progressive traffic, then roll back the release pointer rather than rebuilding production code.
Explain secret handling, provenance, retries, artifact retention, agent loss, and supply-chain compromise.

functional: Register repositories, pipeline definitions, runners, environments, and protected deployment targets.
Run build, unit, integration, security, image, and deployment stages with logs, artifacts, approvals, and status.
Support canary or blue-green rollout, health-based promotion, rollback, cancellation, retention, and audit export.
nonFunctional: Target deployment completion below 10 minutes for a normal service and queue bursts without blocking approvals.
Scale runners by repository and stage, with per-tenant concurrency limits and isolated deployment workers.
Make stage retries and artifact publication idempotent; keep an auditable release history and immutable provenance.
Keep the last known-good version serving when runners, registries, or target clusters are unavailable.
scaleAssumptions: Partition by the primary tenant, user, item, or geographic key and isolate hot partitions.
Keep serving state bounded; retain raw events or durable records for replay and auditing.

deepDives.title: Consistency and idempotency
points: Keep the Complete container CI/CD platform commit authoritative; let derived projections converge with visible version and freshness.
Use idempotency keys, conditional Complete container CI/CD platform writes, event IDs, and versions so retries and replay are safe.
Return Complete container CI/CD platform version and observedAt so clients can reason about freshness.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition Complete container CI/CD platform by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound Complete container CI/CD platform work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.
Keep a replay or reconciliation path for Complete container CI/CD platform projection drift and partial failures.

deepDives.title: Failure and recovery
points: Serve the last acceptable Complete container CI/CD platform projection or an explicit degraded response when workers fail.
Retain durable Complete container CI/CD platform records for replay and make each downstream effect independently retryable.
Measure Complete container CI/CD platform latency, backlog, freshness, error rate, and correctness drift.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.

rubric.description: The answer defines source-triggered builds, gates, artifacts, deployment, scale, durability, and failure contracts.
Entities and revision/run/environment keys support build, test, approvals, deployment, security, and lifecycle changes.
Partitioning, cache behavior, queues, backpressure, and hot-key handling are explicit.
Idempotency, replay, recovery, degraded reads, and observability protect committed state.
The candidate can explain Complete container CI/CD platform consistency, push/pull, managed services, and the scale boundary.
